extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders submitting comments on BLM proposed rules (e.g., recreationists, grazers, industry, tribes, local governments)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments on Bureau of Land Management proposed rules, covering acceptable submission methods, deadlines, privacy/disclosure, and content recommendations (especially for public lands rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for Submitting Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the proposed rule can be submitted via: Federal eRulemaking Portal at http://www.regulations.gov; Personal or messenger delivery; Mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one of the listed submission channels in the notice; follow the instructions in the ADDRESSES section of the proposed rule for where/how to deliver comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Deadlines and Requirements (timeliness and proper address)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice that is open for comment will specify a deadline and methods for submitting comments. The BLM is not obligated to consider or include in the Administrative Record for the final rule: - Comments that are received after the close of the comment period identified in the DATES section of the proposed rule - Comments delivered to an address other than those listed in the ADDRESSES section of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the DATES and ADDRESSES sections of the specific notice; submit comments before the close of the comment period and to the exact addresses provided to ensure BLM will consider them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and Relevance of Comment Content
rubrics_metrics.description: "Make your comments on the proposed rule as specific as possible, confine them to issues pertinent to the proposed rule, and explain the reason for any changes you recommend."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, reference the specific section or paragraph of the proposal that you are addressing; avoid broad or off-topic remarks and explain the rationale behind recommended changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Specific Section or Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, your comments should reference the specific section or paragraph of the proposal that you are addressing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing exact regulatory text locations increases clarity and helps reviewers locate and consider your point; include line/section numbers or quoted language when practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and Disclosure of Personal Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The BLM does not require commenters to disclose their identity when submitting comments on rulemakings. Before including your address, telephone number, email address, or other personal identifying information in your comment, be advised that your entire comment—including your personal identifying information—may be made publicly available at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether to include personal contact details; assume comments (and included personal information) may be posted publicly and redact or omit sensitive personal data if privacy is a concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Your Specific Use or Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Identify your specific use/interest (recreation, grazing, mining, energy, conservation, hunting/fishing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your connection to the affected lands or activities so BLM can assess the relevance and viewpoint of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Specific BLM-Administered Lands by Name and Unit
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Reference specific BLM-administered lands by name and unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the exact land units provides geographic specificity that strengthens comments and helps link issues to local management decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Federal Land Policy and Management Act (FLPMA) Provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Cite Federal Land Policy and Management Act (FLPMA) provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and cite relevant statutory authorities (e.g., FLPMA sections) to frame legal arguments or demonstrate how the proposal aligns or conflicts with statutory mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with NEPA and Endangered Species Act Compliance Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Engage with NEPA/Endangered Species Act compliance issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise specific concerns or support related to environmental analysis, impact assessments, and species protections; provide facts or references to the administrative record where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Local Economic Data
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Provide local economic data (rural community impacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims about economic impacts with quantitative local data (employment, revenue, subsistence use, etc.) to demonstrate how the rule would affect communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Resource Management Plans (RMPs) and Land Use Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Cite Resource Management Plans (RMPs) and Land Use Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant planning documents to show consistency or conflict between the proposed rule and existing land-use decisions or objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Tribal Consultation Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Address tribal consultation considerations where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rule affects tribal interests or lands, discuss consultation history, impacts on tribal resources, and any government-to-government considerations; cite treaties, tribal plans, or consultation records when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame Issues as Multiple-Use vs. Dominant-Use
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Engage with multiple-use vs. dominant-use framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether and why a multiple-use approach or a dominant-use approach is appropriate for the affected lands, and connect that framing to statutory and planning authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Other Relevant Statutes (e.g., Wilderness Act, Wild and Scenic Rivers Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: For public lands rules: Reference Wilderness Act, Wild and Scenic Rivers Act, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite other applicable environmental and land-protection statutes to support legal or policy arguments about protections, designations, or restrictions.
